hypothesis: Question: does the 2011->2012 level shift transfer as a continuing multiplicative growth trend, a plateau, or is it already absorbed by the baseline HGB via the yr feature? Evidence: idea-59da36 (action 2d119fec...) measured internal pseudo-future holdout (cut elapsed_day 425, 61 days) with systematic negative bias for every variant (-54 to -97 rides/hour) and year_level_by_month ratios of 1.84-2.53x, i.e. trees trained mostly on 2011 underpredict later periods and elapsed_day makes it worse (raw|all rmse 115.5 vs raw|no_elapsed_day 95.2). Yet its internally selected sqrt|no_elapsed_day scored dev RMSE 63.04, worse than the plain baseline HGB with all features (idea-baseline-2, 59.99), so a single far-extrapolative holdout misranked candidates; this changed my view: level must be modeled explicitly, and internal selection should use two forward-chained 30-day folds closer to the real train/dev gap and must include the baseline itself as a candidate. Method: HGB on log1p(cnt) using shape features (all except elapsed_day and yr) plus an additive daily log-level offset estimated from cross-fitted (5 contiguous date blocks) out-of-block daily mean residuals; offset for future days is 'none', 'const60' (mean of last 60 training days), 'trend_all' (linear in elapsed_day over all training days) or 'trend180' (linear over last 180 days). Contrasting expected outcomes: (A) trend variants win internally and reduce dev RMSE below 59.99 with pred_mean well above train_mean -> growth continues and is transferable; (B) const60 wins -> level shift transfers as a plateau, trend extrapolation overshoots (positive bias); (C) baseline_all_raw wins or level variants show larger dev RMSE -> the yr indicator already captures the transferable level and residual-level modeling adds noise. Findings report all fold metrics, fitted slopes/constants, the actually selected branch after refitting and any fallback. Unverified exploratory reasoning; a joint change (log target + feature drop + offset), so one-factor attribution is not claimed.
